source.title: No evidence for modulation of the readiness potential by respiratory phase during natural breathing

confidence_rationale: Careful re-analysis (original + new independent dataset + null simulations, Bayesian evidence for absence) that REPLICATES the behavioural expiration clustering of self-initiated actions but shows the neural leg -- respiration modulating the preparatory RP -- is a confound. Mixed for MECH-109: the breath-framed timing of endogenous action survives, but the proposed neural mechanism by which breath would gate preparation is removed, and the authors raise reverse causation (action preparation reshaping breathing).
failure_signatures: Respiratory phase does not modulate readiness-potential amplitude during natural breathing once trials are grouped by phase at movement time; Bayesian analyses favour absence of the effect.

The authors suggest the onset clustering may reflect action preparation changing breathing (a greater I:E ratio, or a respiratory phase reset at trial start) rather than breathing gating preparation, which reverses the causal arrow MECH-109 needs.
Only natural breathing was tested; the paper explicitly leaves open effects under controlled or voluntary breathing, which is the condition MECH-109 is about.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The reported coupling between respiratory phase and RP amplitude arises because both are coupled to movement onset; controlling for this, the coupling disappears. Movements are nonetheless more frequent during expiration (replicated, 13/17 participants).
mapping.ree_translation: Keeps the behavioural premise of MECH-108 (breath frames timing of endogenous actions) while withdrawing the one neural readout previously offered as the gating mechanism. For MECH-109 it sharpens what must be tested: an intervention on breathing, not a correlation with spontaneous phase.
mapping.mapping_caveat: A null on scalp RP amplitude is not a null on respiratory gating of planning in general (hippocampal/limbic entrainment is untouched). Natural breathing only.
mapping.source_context: Healthy adult humans; scalp EEG; Libet-style self-paced movement; re-analysis of Park et al. 2020 data plus a new independent dataset and simulated no-coupling data.

confidence_components.notes: Strong methods paper (independent replication, simulation of the confound, Bayesian nulls). Mapping moderate: bears directly on the evidence base MECH-109 would rely on, not on the voluntary manipulation itself.
